title: Zamzam found again
hookLine: the sirah tells of Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather, digging out the lost well of Zamzam

cards: Dig. That is the whole message, at first, spoken by a voice in a dream to a man asleep near the Ka'ba. Dig what, he asks.
The sirah says the voice came back on other nights, and finally gave him a name, Zamzam, and strange signs for the place: between the dung and the blood, where a crow pecks, near an ants' nest.
The sleeper is Abd al-Muttalib, who would become the grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and he is being told to dig a well Mecca remembered by name, and nobody could find.

teach.b: Zamzam begins long before him. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Abbas tells it. Ibrahim left Hajar and their baby Isma'il in the valley.
The water ran out. Hajar ran between the hills of Safa and Marwa, looking for anyone, until she heard a sound and found an angel digging at the ground, and water came up.

She began holding it in with her hands, building a little basin around it. The Prophet, telling this, said: may Allah have mercy on the mother of Isma'il; if she had left Zamzam alone, it would have been a flowing stream.
In the same report, he says this is why people walk between Safa and Marwa. But wells can be lost.
The sirah says that over time Zamzam was filled in and its place forgotten.

teach.h: A DREAM, A PICKAXE, A SON.
teach.b: Then came the dream. Abd al-Muttalib took a pickaxe and his son al-Harith, his only son at the time, the sirah says, and dug where the signs pointed, until the stones of the old well appeared. Then the hard part.
The men of Quraysh came to him.
This is the well of our father Isma'il, they said; we have a right to it. Give us a share.

teach.h: IT WOULD HAVE BEEN A FLOWING STREAM.
teach.b: He refused. It was given to me, he said, not to you.

The sirah says they set out together to put the quarrel before a judge, and that on the road, when the travelers' water ran out, water sprang up where Abd al-Muttalib's camel rose, and Quraysh gave way.
From then on, giving water to pilgrims was his family's honor, a service the Qur'an itself mentions in surah nine.

how: Pilgrims to Mecca drink Zamzam water and walk between Safa and Marwa in memory of Hajar, and Zamzam water is carried home to share with family and friends.

o: the spring at Medina where caravans watered
the well of Hajar and Isma'il, dug out again
the hill where Hajar ran looking for help

games.q: Zamzam found again — tap the pairs.
p: told in a dream to dig

s: Abd al-Muttalib dug Zamzam for the very first time
the well goes back to Hajar and Isma'il; he found it again.
in the sirah, Quraysh asked for a share of the well
they said it was their father Isma'il's well.
the Prophet said Zamzam would have been a flowing stream if Hajar had left it alone
Ibn Abbas reports it in al-Bukhari.

games.q: you're Abd al-Muttalib. you've just dug out the old well, and the men of Quraysh say: it's our father Isma'il's well, give us a share. what do you do?
o: share it with all of them.
refuse: it was given to you.
fill it back in to end the quarrel.
games.why: the sirah says he refused. they set out for a judge, and on the road, when the water ran out and water sprang up for him, Quraysh gave way.

practice: Let one good thing come up that got filled in over the years, a habit you loved, a friendship, a prayer you used to say, the way the old stones came up under the pickaxe: is there still water there?
If you pray, you can ask Allah to open it again; if you don't, simply remember it, and wonder whether it's worth digging out.

wordCard.voice: Zamzam. The well of Hajar and Isma'il, lost over time, and dug out again by Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the name of the well at Mecca; its meaning is explained in more than one way.

carryVoice: Your line: the old well, found. Tomorrow, a hundred camels. That's day seven hundred three.
